question: What is the medical term for when the tonsils get inflamed and swollen?

options.A: Laryngitis
options.B: Rhinitis
options.C: Tonsillitis
options.D: Pharyngitis

explanation: Correct! Tonsillitis simply means your tonsils are inflamed and fighting off an infection. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h2)

question: What makes a good, clinical patient goal actually useful?

options.A: It must last for at least one full week
options.B: It must be written by the hospital director
options.C: It must be measurable and time-bound
options.D: It must focus solely on spiritual well-being

explanation: A good goal needs to be clear and have a deadline (like 'patient's SpO2 will rise above 95% within 1 hour'). That way, everyone on the ward knows if your care plan is working! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T8#GNS321_U2_T8_h4)

question: When managing an infectious disease, why should a community nurse look beyond just the individual patient?

options.A: Because individual treatments are rarely effective against infections
options.B: To comply with hospital administrative discharge policies
options.C: To prevent the illness from spreading to other members of the community
options.D: Because infectious agents only survive outside the human body

explanation: Great thinking! In community health, we treat the patient while also protecting the wider population from an outbreak. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is local anesthetic WITHOUT epinephrine typically chosen for a skin snip?

options.A: Epinephrine causes severe systemic hypertension
options.B: Epinephrine instantly destroys the surgical scalpel blade
options.C: Local anesthetics cannot be mixed with epinephrine under any rule
options.D: Vasoconstriction can interfere with parasite emergence from the tissue

explanation: Exactly. We want blood vessels to stay open so the tiny live parasites can easily crawl out of the skin sample into our liquid solution. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h3)

question: What causes the intense, driving itch of a scabies mite infestation?

options.A: The mites block blood flow and cause minor tissue death
options.B: An allergic reaction to the mites' waste and proteins in the skin
options.C: The mites chew directly through deep nerve endings
options.D: The mites secrete histamine directly from their mouths

explanation: That severe scabies itch isn't just from crawling—it's your immune system throwing an allergic reaction to the proteins and feces the mites leave behind in their tunnels. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why is practicing injection safety a core professional duty for every nurse?

options.A: Because patients will refuse treatment if nurses lack safety gear
options.B: Because drug manufacturers mandate strict handling instructions
options.C: Because hospital management requires paperwork for every needle used
options.D: Because handling needles always carries a potential window for exposure and infection

explanation: You handle sharps every single day on the ward. Knowing safety rules protects your own health just as much as it protects your patients! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which emergency medication is given during cardiac arrest to narrow blood vessels and boost blood pressure?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Amiodarone
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver; it squeezes peripheral blood vessels so blood gets pushed right where it's needed most: the brain and the heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T7#GNS321_U2_T7_h5)

question: At what fill level should a clinical sharps container be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: Whenever a new nurse starts a shift
options.B: Only at the end of every working week
options.C: When it reaches three-quarters full
options.D: When it is completely packed to the top brim

explanation: Stopping at the three-quarters mark prevents accidental pokes from overflowing needles when dropping items in. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h5)

question: A patient keeps asking you to repeat yourself and turns one ear toward you when you speak. What is your best next nursing action?

options.A: Document that the patient has complete and permanent sensorineural deafness
options.B: Disregard the observation as a normal sign of aging requiring no action
options.C: Perform a focused auditory assessment and check for cerumen impaction
options.D: Refer the patient immediately for urgent visual acuity testing

explanation: Always start with simple nursing assessments first! Looking for a simple wax buildup (cerumen impaction) or checking hearing function is a great practical step before jumping to major conclusions. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h2)

question: How do we tell an indirect obstetric cause of maternal death apart from a direct one?

options.A: It has no relation to the female reproductive system at all
options.B: It only happens during the third trimester of labor
options.C: It is exclusively caused by surgical errors
options.D: It is caused by a pre-existing medical condition worsened by pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Indirect causes are medical issues like heart disease or severe malaria that were already there, but got dangerously worse because of the physical changes of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h4)

question: How does hyperparathyroidism usually impact a patient's bones?

options.A: It forces extra calcium to deposit, making bones overly thick
options.B: It triggers rapid bone growth that crushes nearby nerve roots
options.C: It stops blood flow to the joints, causing cartilage to melt
options.D: It pulls calcium out of bones, making them weak and painful

explanation: Too much parathyroid hormone acts like a withdrawal slip, pulling calcium right out of the skeleton and leaving bones fragile and aching. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h6)

question: A patient gets a drug that blocks opioid receptors and stops other narcotics from binding, but it only causes mild pain relief. What is this called?

options.A: Enzyme inhibitor
options.B: Pure antagonist
options.C: Full agonist
options.D: Partial agonist

explanation: It's a 'partial' player! It grabs the receptor and does a little bit of the job, but not as strongly as a full agonist would. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is pharmacovigilance?

options.A: The clinical trial phase testing drugs on healthy animal subjects
options.B: The mathematical calculation of correct pediatric drug dosages
options.C: The monitoring and prevention of adverse drug reactions
options.D: The process of manufacturing cheap generic pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Pharmacovigilance centers on detecting and tracking adverse drug events to ensure ongoing medication safety. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h6)

question: Which quick bedside test must you do immediately for any unconscious patient?

options.A: Electroencephalogram
options.B: Blood glucose test
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Chest X-ray examination

explanation: Always check the sugar first! Low blood sugar can mimic a major stroke or brain injury, and it's super easy to test and fix right at the bedside. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T9#GNS123_U3_T9_h6)

question: In a fraction, what does the bottom number (the denominator) stand for?

options.A: The total number of equal parts making up the whole
options.B: The maximum adult dose limit
options.C: A metric conversion factor
options.D: The part ordered by the doctor

explanation: Think of a pizza! The denominator at the bottom tells you the total number of slices the whole pizza is cut into. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h2)

question: What is one well-known disadvantage of giving medications rectally?

options.A: Immediate destruction of red blood cells
options.B: Instantaneous and painful liver failure
options.C: Erratic and unpredictable drug absorption
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the anal sphincter

explanation: Because of stool, different blood flow rates, or early expulsion, rectal drugs don't always absorb as steadily as intravenous medications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary action of vasopressor medications like norepinephrine in shock?

options.A: Dissolve blood clots in the coronary arteries
options.B: Dilate the bronchial tubes in the lungs
options.C: Slow down a rapid heart rate
options.D: Constrict blood vessels to raise blood pressure

explanation: Vasopressors cause blood vessels to tighten, which increases vascular resistance and helps raise blood pressure when fluids are not enough. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h6)

question: How many minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise are generally recommended per week for cardiovascular health?

options.A: At least 75 minutes
options.B: At least 150 minutes
options.C: At least 500 minutes
options.D: At least 300 minutes

explanation: Standard health guidelines recommend a minimum of 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly to maintain heart health and lower disease risk. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h4)

question: Which nursing action compromises the accuracy of a fluid balance chart?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to guess and write down intake amounts
options.B: Involving the patient and family in reporting oral drinks
options.C: Converting all cup and bowl volumes into milliliters promptly
options.D: Notifying the doctor immediately about a sudden drop in urine output

explanation: Relying on memory causes missed entries and incorrect data that jeopardize patient safety. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h8)

question: What term describes the dangerous point where two or more organ systems fail during severe, prolonged shock?

options.A: Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome
options.B: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
options.C: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
options.D: Systemic Vascular Resistance Failure

explanation: MODS is what happens when severe shock goes on too long unchecked: the whole body cascade causes organs like the kidneys, lungs, and liver to start shutting down one by one. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h8)

question: Which symptom makes eating and drinking very dangerous for patients with advanced degenerative disorders?

options.A: Permanent loss of taste
options.B: Excessive salivation
options.C: Rapid tooth enamel growth
options.D: Severe dysphagia

explanation: Dysphagia is the medical term for trouble swallowing. It puts patients at a high risk of choking or getting food into their lungs. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h5)

question: Which vital sign must you keep a close eye on continuously during a laryngoscopy?

options.A: Urine output
options.B: Blood glucose
options.C: Pulse oximetry
options.D: Core body temperature

explanation: Spot on! Because we are working right in the airway, watching oxygen levels closely ensures the patient is getting enough air the whole time. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is a common challenge that ruins a good nursing handover?

options.A: Using the SBAR framework correctly
options.B: Noise, distractions, and staff fatigue
options.C: Having too many standardized reporting templates
options.D: Patients being fully awake and cooperative

explanation: When people are tired and the ward is noisy, it's super easy to miss crucial details during report. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h8)

question: Why should you ask a patient to close their eyes during a sensory touch test?

options.A: To measure if the patient can stay awake under stress
options.B: To prevent visual cues from helping them guess the stimulus
options.C: To help the patient fall asleep during a long examination
options.D: To protect the eyes from bright room lights and glare

explanation: Closing their eyes ensures they rely purely on their nerves and touch, rather than cheating by peeking at what you are doing! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which drug class is mainly used to calm down severe leprosy reactions and save nerves from permanent damage?

options.A: Antifungal agents
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Corticosteroids
options.D: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Correct! Corticosteroids like prednisolone are superstars at calming down dangerous inflammation during leprosy flare-ups. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T5#GNS213_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the core focus of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) when managing chronic health conditions?

options.A: Changing unhelpful thought patterns and building practical coping skills
options.B: Using high doses of medication to alter brain chemistry permanently
options.C: Healing past childhood trauma unrelated to the current illness
options.D: Physically strengthening damaged muscle fibers through exercise

explanation: CBT is all about spotting negative thoughts and swapping them for healthy coping habits to make everyday life a little easier. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h4)

question: Why does infection inside a bone cause tissue death much faster than infections in soft tissue?

options.A: Bone is trapped inside a rigid structure where swelling cuts off its blood supply
options.B: The periosteum actively feeds the bacteria instead of protecting the bone
options.C: Bones lack white blood cells entirely to fight off invading bacteria
options.D: Microorganisms multiply twice as fast inside hard calcium deposits

explanation: Because bone cannot expand, swelling and pus create high pressure inside the rigid bone cavity, which compresses blood vessels and starves the tissue of oxygen. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: What is a major reason why clients sometimes stop using modern contraceptives early?

options.A: Sudden nationwide shortages of barrier supplies
options.B: Automatic expiration of contraceptive efficacy after one month
options.C: Anxiety and fear regarding normal physiological side effects
options.D: Mandatory government limits on the duration of use

explanation: Spot on! Many clients stop using a method when they notice minor changes like spotting simply because nobody warned them it's a normal body reaction. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h5)

question: In aeromedical work, what does the safety acronym 'CRM' stand for?

options.A: Certified Rescue Medic
options.B: Crew Resource Management
options.C: Clinical Risk Method
options.D: Critical Respiratory Monitoring

explanation: You've got this! CRM is a fantastic aviation safety framework that encourages teamwork, clear communication, and shared problem-solving among everyone on board. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T14#GNS321_U2_T14_h8)

question: When does bereavement support provided by the healthcare team typically take place?

options.A: It stops the exact moment the patient's heart stops beating
options.B: It continues for a period of time after the patient's death
options.C: It starts only if the family requests financial assistance
options.D: It begins only after the funeral service is completely finished

explanation: Bereavement care supports grieving family members in the days, weeks, and months following their loved one's passing. Nursing care goes beyond the bedside! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h8)

question: What is the main benefit of placing a patient in the lateral (side-lying) position?

options.A: It maximizes lung expansion for asthma attacks
options.B: It takes weight off the sacrum and heels
options.C: It allows the patient to eat solid food safely
options.D: It provides direct access for urinary catheter insertion

explanation: Rolling a patient onto their side takes heavy pressure off the tailbone and heels, keeping their skin safe from bedsores! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is a major benefit of encouraging male partner involvement in PMTCT programs?

options.A: It improves clinic attendance and supports maternal drug adherence.
options.B: It removes the responsibility of health education from the nurse.
options.C: It allows fathers to breastfeed the infant during the night.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for infant diagnostic testing.

explanation: When male partners are involved and supportive, mothers find it easier to keep appointments and take their medications consistently. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h8)

question: Why do many teenage girls experience irregular periods shortly after starting menstruation?

options.A: Poor nutrition always disrupts adolescent cycles
options.B: The brain-to-ovary hormone pathway is still maturing
options.C: They lack sufficient body fat for hormones
options.D: Endometrial tissue is not fully formed yet

explanation: Just like learning to ride a bicycle, the brain and ovaries take a couple of years to sync up their chemical communication after a girl's first period. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is a valid medical reason to put in an indwelling urinary catheter?

options.A: General urinary incontinence with no skin breakdown
options.B: To make things easier for nursing staff during busy night shifts
options.C: Accurate hourly urine output measurement in a critically ill patient
options.D: The patient prefers not to get up to use the toilet at night

explanation: Spot on! We only use indwelling catheters when there is a strong medical need, like closely tracking kidney function in very sick patients. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h4)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary in palliative care?

options.A: To reduce the number of working hours for individual doctors
options.B: Because physical, emotional, and social needs require diverse expert skills
options.C: To ensure that family members never have to help at home
options.D: Because hospital regulations legally mandate large staffing numbers

explanation: It takes a village! Since a serious illness affects the body, mind, and soul, we need different experts—doctors, nurses, social workers, and chaplains—working as a team. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T2#GNS321_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is considered the absolute cornerstone of youth-friendly healthcare?

options.A: Formal hospital uniforms
options.B: Expensive equipment
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Strict parental control

explanation: Guarantees of privacy and confidentiality are essential to make young people feel safe enough to share personal health details. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h7)

question: Why are chemotherapy drugs considered dangerous for the nurses who handle them?

options.A: They always emit a poisonous gas that fills the entire hospital ward
options.B: They are designed to kill cells and can harm the nurse's cellular health
options.C: They cause immediate fainting if the nurse smells them
options.D: They instantly burn through standard hospital uniforms and skin

explanation: Chemo drugs work by destroying cells. That makes them powerful treatments for patients, but it also means nurses must handle them with extreme care to avoid toxic exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which of these is a key way your blood helps regulate your body?

options.A: Maintaining normal body temperature
options.B: Generating electrical impulses for the heart
options.C: Synthesizing new digestive enzymes
options.D: Producing red bone marrow stem cells

explanation: Well done! Blood acts like a personal heating system, picking up heat from active muscles and sharing it around the body to keep you at a steady, safe temperature. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T1#GNS311_U2_T1_h2)

question: A nurse is getting the tray ready for a sigmoidoscopy. Which tool is needed if the doctor wants to take a sample of a suspicious spot?

options.A: An IV infusion pump
options.B: A urinary catheter
options.C: A rigid speculum
options.D: Biopsy forceps

explanation: Awesome! Biopsy forceps slide right through the scope to pinch a tiny, painless tissue sample for the lab to check. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T6#GNS221_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which blood product is usually given to replace multiple missing clotting factors in a patient with severe liver disease?

options.A: Packed red blood cells
options.B: Normal saline solution
options.C: Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP)
options.D: Ringer's lactate solution

explanation: Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) is packed with all the liquid plasma proteins and clotting factors a failing liver can no longer make on its own. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T11#GNS311_U2_T11_h7)

question: What is the recommended alternative if a patient with a cough does not have a tissue available?

options.A: Covering the mouth with a shared towel
options.B: Coughing into the inner elbow
options.C: Turning their head toward the nurse
options.D: Coughing directly into their bare hands

explanation: Coughing into the elbow prevents respiratory droplets from contaminating the hands, which easily transfer germs to surfaces and other people. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: In a healthy human body, where do normal prion proteins naturally live?

options.A: Along the lining of the gut
options.B: On the membranes of neurons
options.C: Inside red blood cells
options.D: Within the fluid of joints

explanation: You got it! Normal prions hang out peacefully on the surface membranes of our nerve cells. It's only when they change shape that trouble starts. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h2)

question: After cleaning the skin with an antiseptic and before giving the numbing injection, what is the next important step?

options.A: Suturing the edges of the anticipated wound
options.B: Placing sterile surgical drapes over the patient
options.C: Applying direct pressure to collapse blood vessels
options.D: Allowing the antiseptic solution to dry completely

explanation: Patience is key! Antiseptics need a little air-drying time to actually kill the germs before the skin barrier is opened up. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T3#GNS213_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which nursing action is most important for tracking fluid buildup in a patient with heart inflammation?

options.A: Doing reflex checks on both arms
options.B: Checking the patient's vision every four hours
options.C: Testing grip strength twice a day
options.D: Checking daily weights and tracking intake and output

explanation: Tracking daily weights and fluid charts is your best early warning system for fluid retention and failing heart function. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: What does MODS stand for in the context of prolonged shock?

options.A: Massive Oxygen Deprivation State
options.B: Multi-Organ Dysfunction Syndrome
options.C: Myocardial Obstruction Disease Syndrome
options.D: Metabolic Overload and Destruction System

explanation: MODS refers to the progressive failure of two or more organ systems resulting from severe, uncorrected systemic shock. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h9)

question: What is the best way to confirm if a patient has a drug allergy before giving a new medication?

options.A: Wait until after the drug is given to see if a rash appears
options.B: Assume they have no allergies if they look healthy and calm
options.C: Ask the conscious patient directly and check their written chart
options.D: Ask another patient sharing the same ward room for confirmation

explanation: The safest approach is to talk directly with the patient and cross-check their written chart. Never guess when it comes to allergies! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the medical term for inflammation of the external female genitalia?

options.A: Endometritis
options.B: Cervicitis
options.C: Salpingitis
options.D: Vulvitis

explanation: Vulvitis specifically refers to the inflammation of the external female structures making up the vulva. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h1)

question: How does the World Health Organization (WHO) officially define health?

options.A: The total absence of any infection or physical pain
options.B: The ability to work and function normally in society
options.C: A balance between spiritual and biological body forces
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being

explanation: You've got this! The WHO looks at the whole person. Health isn't just about a strong body; it includes how we feel mentally and how we relate to others around us. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h1)

question: A patient with a heavy leg cast reports a tingling sensation and toes that feel cold. Which nursing diagnosis is most urgent here?

options.A: Impaired Skin Integrity
options.B: Ineffective Health Maintenance
options.C: Risk for Activity Intolerance
options.D: Risk for Peripheral Neurovascular Dysfunction

explanation: Cold toes and tingling indicate compromised blood flow or nerve pressure, making neurovascular protection the highest priority. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h4)

question: What is the primary reason for establishing trust during a genitourinary assessment?

options.A: To eliminate the requirement for formal medical documentation
options.B: To prevent the need for diagnostic laboratory tests
options.C: To speed up the physical examination process
options.D: To encourage the patient to share sensitive health details

explanation: Genitourinary symptoms involve private bodily functions, making trust essential for an honest and accurate patient history. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h1)

question: What antibodies are found in the plasma of a person with Type AB blood?

options.A: Both anti-A and anti-B antibodies
options.B: Only anti-B antibodies
options.C: Neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies
options.D: Only anti-A antibodies

explanation: Type AB blood has both A and B antigens on the cells, so the body does not make antibodies against either one, or it would attack its own blood. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why are patients who suffer massive insect stings at risk for sudden kidney injury?

options.A: Profound low blood pressure and direct venom toxicity compromise renal perfusion
options.B: Patients refuse to drink water due to fear of swallowing
options.C: Venom causes direct physical blockage of the ureters by crystals
options.D: The kidneys work overtime to filter out oral antihistamine pills

explanation: Spot on! Severe shock starves the kidneys of blood flow, and heavy venom toxins can directly damage the delicate kidney tubules. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T12#GNS221_U3_T12_h7)

question: How do standard hormonal emergency contraceptive pills stop a pregnancy from happening?

options.A: By destroying a fertilized egg that is already implanted
options.B: By permanently stopping the normal production of estrogen
options.C: By thickening the bladder lining to trap excess hormones
options.D: By delaying or preventing the release of an egg from the ovary

explanation: Hormonal emergency pills simply hit the pause button on ovulation. If no egg is released, the sperm has nothing to fertilize. Simple and clever! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T021#GNS226_U6_T021_h3)

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main duties when it comes to environmental health?

options.A: Paving dirt roads to prevent dust inhalation in villages
options.B: Manufacturing chemical disinfectants in pharmaceutical labs
options.C: Educating patients and communities on hygiene practices
options.D: Constructing modern sewage treatment plants for cities

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Teaching patients how to keep their homes and habits clean is a huge part of community health nursing. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h7)

question: A stroke patient is resting in bed for a long time without moving. What major leg complication are they most at risk for?

options.A: Peripheral neuropathy
options.B: Arterial plaque regression
options.C: Chronic bone demineralization
options.D: Deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Spot on! When a patient cannot move well, blood pools in the lower legs, putting them at high risk for deep vein thrombosis (DVT). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of priming extension tubing with normal saline before starting an IV?

options.A: To remove trapped air and prevent air embolisms
options.B: To warm the tubing up to body temperature
options.C: To test if the syringe plunger moves smoothly
options.D: To dilute any medication given later on

explanation: Clearing all air bubbles from the line stops air from entering the patient's bloodstream during cannulation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand normal female anatomy and physiology?

options.A: To diagnose rare genetic abnormalities routinely
options.B: To tell healthy development apart from actual illness
options.C: To prevent natural menopause from happening
options.D: To prescribe hormone therapy for every patient

explanation: Spotting what's normal is your superpower as a nurse! Once you know what a healthy cycle or transition looks like, you can easily catch when something needs medical attention. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h1)

question: What mental health challenge do rehabilitation psychologists most commonly help patients work through?

options.A: Physical balance and dizziness
options.B: Nutritional deficits and tube-feeding routines
options.C: Managing acute surgical site pain
options.D: Coping with a sudden disability and grief

explanation: A life-altering illness or injury brings deep emotional pain. Rehab psychologists help patients process these feelings and adapt to their new reality. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T3#GNS123_U6_T3_h7)

question: What is the purpose of adding hyaluronic acid to an arthritic joint?

options.A: To permanently numb the nerves of the entire leg
options.B: To kill bacterial infections inside the joint capsule
options.C: To permanently fuse the joint bones together
options.D: To act as a viscosupplement and improve joint lubrication

explanation: Hyaluronic acid mimics natural joint fluid to provide cushioning and smooth movement. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: Along with classic symptoms, what random blood sugar level usually points toward diabetes?

options.A: 200 mg/dL or higher
options.B: 120 to 139 mg/dL
options.C: 90 to 110 mg/dL
options.D: 50 to 70 mg/dL

explanation: An RBS reading of 200 mg/dL or more, paired with signs like extreme thirst and frequent urination, is a strong red flag for diabetes. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T19#GNS222_U2_T19_h5)

question: How is a patient usually positioned immediately after a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Flat in bed
options.B: Trendelenburg position
options.C: High Fowler's position
options.D: Standing up and walking

options.B: Strict bed rest and fluid restriction
options.C: Surgical excision
options.D: Long-term oral antibiotic therapy

explanation: Since it's a physical mass, the best way to deal with a benign heart tumour is to surgically cut it out. Clean and effective! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h6)

question: Which of these is a common body trigger that can cause a seizure?

options.A: High iron levels
options.B: Excess vitamin C
options.C: Low blood sugar
options.D: Low dietary fiber

explanation: Correct! When blood sugar drops too low (hypoglycemia), brain cells are robbed of their fuel and can trigger a seizure. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T10#GNS222_U4_T10_h4)

question: A patient in the recovery room suddenly has low blood pressure, a fast pulse, and pale, cool skin. What is the most likely problem?

options.A: Normal recovery from muscle relaxants
options.B: Hypertension caused by room temperature
options.C: Hemorrhage and developing shock
options.D: Severe allergic reaction to hospital linen

explanation: Low blood pressure, a racing heart, and cool skin are classic warning signs that the patient might be bleeding internally (hemorrhage) and going into shock. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T10#GNS123_U5_T10_h4)

question: What type of thinking skills usually show up during middle adolescence?

options.A: Fully mature adult executive reasoning
options.B: Formal operational or abstract thinking
options.C: Pre-operational magical thinking
options.D: Only concrete operational thinking

explanation: Well done! Middle adolescents start thinking beyond what's right in front of them—they can grasp abstract ideas and imagine 'what if' scenarios. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main difference between microvascular and macrovascular diabetic complications?

options.A: If the condition affects the upper or lower body
options.B: Whether the patient feels pain or numbness
options.C: The size of the damaged blood vessels
options.D: How fast the symptoms appear after a meal

explanation: It's all in the name! Micro means tiny vessels (like in the eyes and kidneys), while macro means larger arteries (like heart and brain vessels). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h7)

question: What percentage of total blood volume is typically made up of plasma?

options.A: 45 percent
options.B: 20 percent
options.C: 55 percent
options.D: 80 percent

explanation: Plasma makes up about 55 percent of your blood. It acts as the liquid highway carrying cells, nutrients, and waste products all around the body! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h2)

question: How does General Paralysis of the Insane (GPI) usually show up in a patient?

options.A: It strikes suddenly right after a head injury.
options.B: It appears a few days after a bad cough or cold.
options.C: It is passed down directly from parents to children in their genes.
options.D: It develops many years after an untreated syphilis infection.

explanation: Spot on! GPI is a late complication of neurosyphilis that quietly creeps in years or even decades after the initial infection was missed or left untreated. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h1)

question: What are the two main components that make up human consciousness?

options.A: Memory and speech
options.B: Wakefulness and awareness
options.C: Sensation and movement
options.D: Reflexes and coordination

explanation: Consciousness is defined clinically by a person's physical wakefulness and their cognitive awareness of themselves and the environment. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h1)

question: What does 'anticipatory grief' mean for caregivers of patients with degenerative illnesses?

options.A: Grief felt in advance as they watch their loved one slowly decline
options.B: Anger at the medical team for failing to find a genetic cure
options.C: Relief that the patient's physical illness will soon be over
options.D: Confusion about how to fill out insurance and hospital forms

explanation: Spot on. Caregivers often mourn the gradual loss of their loved one's personality and skills long before the person actually passes away. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h6)

question: What is the main medication used to treat General Paralysis of the Insane?

options.A: Corticosteroid shots
options.B: Intravenous Penicillin G
options.C: Oral antiviral tablets
options.D: Insulin injections

explanation: Well done! High-dose intravenous penicillin G is our top weapon to clear the Treponema pallidum bacteria out of the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T1#GNS222_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why are accurate nursing records about needle counts so important in a court of law?

options.A: They show how fast the surgical team can work
options.B: They prove that standard safety protocols were followed
options.C: They help the hospital calculate patient food bills
options.D: They determine the salary of the operating theatre staff

explanation: You're doing great! Clear charting is your best legal protection, proving you did your job safely and correctly. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h6)

question: What is a major reason for giving a neuromuscular blocker during emergency intubation?

options.A: To relax vocal cords and jaw muscles for safe tube placement
options.B: To help the patient clear thick mucus secretions from the lungs
options.C: To stimulate the patient to breathe deeply on their own without help
options.D: To instantly reverse dangerous drops in systemic blood pressure

explanation: Relaxing the jaw and vocal cords makes sliding the breathing tube in much smoother, protecting the patient's airway and throat from trauma. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h3)
